title: Day 1 Knowledge Check: Classical ML Baseline

questions.question: Why build a TF-IDF + LogisticRegression baseline on Day 1 before deploying an SLM?

options.A: To establish a deterministic latency/accuracy floor and verify whether simpler ML solves the task at zero token cost.
options.B: Because Qdrant requires TF-IDF weights to initialize.
options.C: Because Hugging Face models cannot classify P1/P2/P3 labels.

questions.explanation: A classical ML floor runs in <5ms with zero GPU/token cost and proves where semantic LLMs add real value.
questions.implication: Skipping a classical baseline in production often leads to over-engineered, high-latency LLM pipelines for problems solvable with simple classifiers.

questions.question: What is the primary limitation of TF-IDF bag-of-words on unseen production alerts?

options.A: It cannot run offline on Windows.
options.B: It relies on exact lexical overlap and misses semantic synonyms (e.g., 'RAM exhausted' vs 'OOMKilled').
options.C: It always takes more than 2 seconds per query.

questions.explanation: TF-IDF tracks exact n-grams; semantic embeddings (Day 2) solve synonym matching.
questions.implication: When on-call services emit slightly different phrasing for the same failure mode, pure keyword models suffer silent false negatives.

questions.question: Where are runtime URLs and the default domain configured in this repository?

options.A: Hardcoded inside Cell 4 of each notebook.
options.B: Centralized in .env and configs/app_config.yaml via engine/settings.py.

questions.explanation: AppSettings in engine/settings.py externalizes all URLs, model paths, and domain profiles.
questions.implication: Externalizing configuration lets you promote identical code from local Windows laptops to GCP Cloud Run or AWS ECS with zero code edits.
